It has also been referred to as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” although that refers to it being the largest shrine in the local area, not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province. == Enshrined Deities == [[File:片野神社RIMG2186.JPG|thumb|right|Torii]] * Main Enshrined Deities: Takehayasusanoo no Ōkami (Susanoo), Sugawara no Michizane * Additional deities: Kushinadahime no Mikoto, Yashima Shinumi no Kami Due to the Meiji-era consolidation of nearby shrines, several other deities have been added, resulting in multiple enshrined Hachiman gods (total of four) and others. The Kokka (family records) of the shrine’s priestly family, the Okada family, refers to it as “the tutelary of the Haji (土師) clan.” Some old references associate its deity with Nigihayahi no Mikoto or the ancestor of the Katanoinagi clan, but the shrine denies these identifications. == History == [[File:河内名所図会 交野神社.png|thumb|From “Kawachi Meisho Zue”: Katanoinagi Jinja (Katano Jinja)]] According to shrine tradition, during the era of Emperor Suinin, Nomino Sukune, a noble from Izumo, received this land as a reward for victory in a sumo match against Taima no Kehaya. He then enshrined his ancestral deity Susanoo at this location as a clan’s tutelary deity.{{Cite web|url=https://www.katanojinja.com/blank-3|title=History|publisher=Katano Jinja|access-date=2024-06-02}} During Emperor Kinmei’s time, the shrine was renamed “Katano Jinja” after the local area “Katano” (also known as “Katano” or “Kawachi”), giving rise to the name of Katano District and eventually Hirakata City. Thus, it served as the ubusuna (local tutelary) shrine of Katano District. In the mid-Heian period, after Sugawara no Michizane (a descendant of the Haji clan) was enshrined as a kami (Tenjin), he was added here as well in Tennin 4 (960). The Okada family, who serve as shrine priests, are said to be descendants of Nomino Sukune. Listed in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō as “Katanojinja, Kuwajutsu,” it was a small Shikinaisha. It once had extensive shrine lands and was famed for its cherry blossoms (“Makino no sakura”) making it a utamakura (poetic place name). Because it was a large shrine in Katano District, in the late Heian period the shrine’s name was changed to “Ichinomiya.” This led to it being known as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” but it was not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province—rather, it was the ichinomiya of Katano District. During the Genkō War (Nanboku-chō period), it was burned but later rebuilt. In the Sengoku period, it suffered damage due to involvement in battles between the Miyoshi Sanninshū and Matsunaga Hisahide but was restored in Tenshō 11 (1583) by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who regarded it as the guardian against the demon gate (kimon) for Osaka Castle. Later, in Keichō 7 (1602), Toyotomi Hideyori rebuilt the main hall and associated buildings. During the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to Gozu Tennō and was officially named “Ichinomiya Gozu Tennō.” In the Meiji era, when merging shrines in former Makino Village, it reverted to its old name “Katano Jinja” and was ranked as a gōsha under the modern shrine system. === Meiji-era Shrines Merger === In the Meiji era, the following shrines in the old Makino Village were merged into Katano Jinja: * Awakura Jinja (Ōaza Ogura; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Kudaraō Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Kudaraō no Mikoto & Susanoo. Note: Different from the middle shrine Kudaraō Jinja) * Mikari Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Ōsazaki no Mikoto, Kudaraō, Susanoo) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Ibojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Kamijima; Deities: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]], Amaterasu Ōmikami, Amenokoyane no Mikoto) * Hachiman Jinja (Ōaza Shimojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Uyama; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Dōso Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kunanodo no Kami) * Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kususumi no Ōkami) Because of its historical role as a protector of Osaka Castle’s “kimon” direction, Katano Jinja remains revered for hōyoke (warding off evil directions) and yakuyoke (warding off misfortune). The “oni” (demon) is regarded as a symbol and guardian deity of the shrine due to these associations, leading to unique customs such as “Oni wa uchi!” (“Demons come in!”) instead of “Oni wa soto!” (“Demons out!”) during Setsubun bean-throwing rituals, and oni motifs appearing on ema and goshuin. === Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja === Kususumi Jinja, a Shikinaisha, was merged in 1909. Formerly the ujigami of Kyū坂 Village, it was located about where Makinohommachi 1-chome 7 is now. Its deity was “Kususumi no Ōkami.” The shrine’s signpost now stands in the woods within Katano Jinja. The relationship between this shrine and a similarly named shrine in Yamato Province is unknown. === Aterui and More’s Mound === Adjacent north of the shrine grounds is Makino Park, formerly part of the shrine’s land. A mound in the center of this park is traditionally said to be the Kofun (head mound) of Aterui (Aterui no kubizuka).{{Cite book|language=ja|editor=Hirakata City Board of Education|title=Tanoshiku Manabu Hirakata no Rekishi (Enjoyable Study of Hirakata’s History)|publisher=Hirakata City Board of Education|year=2006-03-31|id=JP:21124110}} In 1979, the Kahoku Shinpo newspaper reported that local tradition has long held that a major defeated general’s head was buried here, and about 1 km northeast in Uyama-chō, another old mound was found with similar legends.{{Cite news|language=ja|title=Is the Emishi chieftain buried here? Aterui’s execution site and burial place found in Osaka’s Hirakata; Locals strive to preserve it|newspaper=Kahoku Shinpo|date=1979-03-25|edition=12th|page=18}} In 2007, a stone monument reading “Den Aterui More no Zuka” (Mound of Aterui and More) was erected. The shrine also sells Aterui omamori charms symbolizing friendship and ties, referencing the legendary stories of friendship and rivalry between Aterui and Sakanoue no Tamuramaro. == Buildings and Cultural Properties == * Honden (main hall) (Important Cultural Property) - Rebuilt in Keichō 7 (1602) by Toyotomi Hideyori with Katagiri Katsumoto as overseer. A sangensha nagare-zukuri style, hinoki cypress bark roof.{{Cite book|language=ja|title=Hirakata-shi no Shaji Kenchiku (Temple and Shrine Architecture in Hirakata)|publisher=Hirakata City Board of Education|series=Hirakata City Building Survey Report III|year=1994-03-31|id=JP:97035268|pages=34-40|chapter=Katano Jinja}} * Haiden (Worship Hall) - Also rebuilt by Toyotomi Hideyori in Keichō 7 (1602). * Stone lantern (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - From the late Kamakura period, believed to belong to the former Jingū-ji of the shrine. * East Gate (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - Also called Kuro-mon. A Yotsuashimon (four-legged gate) originally built in the late Muromachi period. * South Gate (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - Also called Aka-mon. Rebuilt by Toyotomi Hideyori in Keichō 7 (1602) as a yotsuashimon with hongawara roofing. Hirakata_Katano_Shrine_Honden.jpeg|Honden (Important Cultural Property) Katano-jinja_Haiden.jpg|Inside the Haiden Monument of Aterui in Hirakata.jpeg|"Den Aterui More no Zuka" monument == Subordinate Shrines == === On-site Subsidiaries === [[File:Katano-jinja Yorihimesha.jpg|thumb|160px|Yorihime-sha (on-site subsidiary)]] [[File:Katano-jinja Kusagamisha.jpg|thumb|160px|Kusagami-sha (off-site shrine)]] * Inari-sha - Deities: Ukemochi no Kami, Takemikazuchi no Kami, Futsunushi no Kami, Amenokoyane no Mikoto, Hime no Ōkami, [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]], Kunanodo no Kami * Yorihime-sha - Deities: Tamayorihime no Mikoto, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto, Ichikishimahime no Mikoto === Off-site Subsidiaries === Both located east of the main precincts, separated by the Hirakata East Fire Station Saka Branch: * Asahara Jinja - deity: Sarutahiko no Mikoto. Guardian for travel safety and descendant prosperity. * Kusagami-sha - deity: HiwasuSeri no Mikoto ** According to legend, when Sugawara no Michizane was en route to Dazaifu, his horse fell ill and died here, subsequently revered by locals and associated with healing skin diseases due to a pun on “kusa” (grass) and “kusa” (lesion). == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Property (National) === * Honden (including one wooden tablet) - Dated “Rebuilt in Keichō 7 (1602) 11th Month.” === Osaka Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties === * Katano Jinja: East Gate, South Gate * Stone Lantern (from late Kamakura period) == location == * location: 2-21-15 Makinosaka, Hirakata City, Osaka Prefecture == Access == * About 5 minutes’ walk east from [[Makino Station (Keihan)|Makino Station]] on the Keihan Main Line == Notes == {{Reflist|2}} == References == {{More footnotes|date=June 2024}} * Katano Jinja Ryakuki (summary booklet available at the shrine) * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Okada Momoko|title=Jinja Wakaoku Nikki: Torii wo Kugureba Betsekai (A Young Shrine Wife’s Diary)|publisher=Shodensha Kōbunko|date=2004-01|isbn=4-396-31339-X}} == Related Items == * [[Hiraoka Shrine]] - {{ill|Hyōsu-jinja|ja|兵主神社 (西脇市)|12=draft|12=draft}} |religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Katano Jinja | image = [[image:Katano Shrine, Hirakata Haiden 2006.jpg|250px]]
Haiden (worship hall) | caption = | map_type = Japan Osaka | coordinates = {{Coord|34|50|30.5|N|135|40|03.5|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Katano Jinja}} | location = 2-21-15 Makinosaka, {{ill|Hirakata, Osaka|ja|枚方市|lt=Hirakata City|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|lt=Osaka Prefecture|12=draft|12=draft}} | deity = {{ubl|Takehayasusanoo no Ōkami (Susanoo)|Sugawara no Michizane}} | type = {{ubl|Shikinaisha (small)|(Reputed) Kawashū Ichinomiya|Former Gōsha}} | founded = Era of Emperor Suinin | honden = Sangensha nagare-zukuri style | festival = October 15 | ceremonies = {{ubl|Ohitaki-sai (Mikan throwing) on Dec.13|Ebisu-sai Jan.9–11}} }} '''Katano Jinja''' (片埜神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Hirakata, Osaka|ja|枚方市|lt=Hirakata City|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|lt=Osaka Prefecture|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a Shikinaisha (small) shrine with an old shrine rank of gōsha. It has also been referred to as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” although that refers to it being the largest shrine in the local area, not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province. == Enshrined Deities == [[File:片野神社RIMG2186.JPG|thumb|right|Torii]] * Main Enshrined Deities: Takehayasusanoo no Ōkami (Susanoo), Sugawara no Michizane * Additional deities: Kushinadahime no Mikoto, Yashima Shinumi no Kami Due to the Meiji-era consolidation of nearby shrines, several other deities have been added, resulting in multiple enshrined Hachiman gods (total of four) and others. The Kokka (family records) of the shrine’s priestly family, the Okada family, refers to it as “the tutelary of the Haji (土師) clan.” Some old references associate its deity with Nigihayahi no Mikoto or the ancestor of the Katanoinagi clan, but the shrine denies these identifications. == History == [[File:河内名所図会 交野神社.png|thumb|From “Kawachi Meisho Zue”: Katanoinagi Jinja (Katano Jinja)]] According to shrine tradition, during the era of Emperor Suinin, Nomino Sukune, a noble from Izumo, received this land as a reward for victory in a sumo match against Taima no Kehaya. He then enshrined his ancestral deity Susanoo at this location as a clan’s tutelary deity.{{Cite web|url=https://www.katanojinja.com/blank-3|title=History|publisher=Katano Jinja|access-date=2024-06-02}} During Emperor Kinmei’s time, the shrine was renamed “Katano Jinja” after the local area “Katano” (also known as “Katano” or “Kawachi”), giving rise to the name of Katano District and eventually Hirakata City. Thus, it served as the ubusuna (local tutelary) shrine of Katano District. In the mid-Heian period, after Sugawara no Michizane (a descendant of the Haji clan) was enshrined as a kami (Tenjin), he was added here as well in Tennin 4 (960). The Okada family, who serve as shrine priests, are said to be descendants of Nomino Sukune. Listed in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō as “Katanojinja, Kuwajutsu,” it was a small Shikinaisha. It once had extensive shrine lands and was famed for its cherry blossoms (“Makino no sakura”) making it a utamakura (poetic place name). Because it was a large shrine in Katano District, in the late Heian period the shrine’s name was changed to “Ichinomiya.” This led to it being known as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” but it was not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province—rather, it was the ichinomiya of Katano District. During the Genkō War (Nanboku-chō period), it was burned but later rebuilt. In the Sengoku period, it suffered damage due to involvement in battles between the Miyoshi Sanninshū and Matsunaga Hisahide but was restored in Tenshō 11 (1583) by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who regarded it as the guardian against the demon gate (kimon) for Osaka Castle. Later, in Keichō 7 (1602), Toyotomi Hideyori rebuilt the main hall and associated buildings. During the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to Gozu Tennō and was officially named “Ichinomiya Gozu Tennō.” In the Meiji era, when merging shrines in former Makino Village, it reverted to its old name “Katano Jinja” and was ranked as a gōsha under the modern shrine system. === Meiji-era Shrines Merger === In the Meiji era, the following shrines in the old Makino Village were merged into Katano Jinja: * Awakura Jinja (Ōaza Ogura; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Kudaraō Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Kudaraō no Mikoto & Susanoo. Note: Different from the middle shrine Kudaraō Jinja) * Mikari Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Ōsazaki no Mikoto, Kudaraō, Susanoo) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Ibojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Kamijima; Deities: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]], Amaterasu Ōmikami, Amenokoyane no Mikoto) * Hachiman Jinja (Ōaza Shimojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Uyama; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Dōso Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kunanodo no Kami) * Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kususumi no Ōkami) Because of its historical role as a protector of Osaka Castle’s “kimon” direction, Katano Jinja remains revered for hōyoke (warding off evil directions) and yakuyoke (warding off misfortune). The “oni” (demon) is regarded as a symbol and guardian deity of the shrine due to these associations, leading to unique customs such as “Oni wa uchi!” (“Demons come in!”) instead of “Oni wa soto!” (“Demons out!”) during Setsubun bean-throwing rituals, and oni motifs appearing on ema and goshuin. === Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja === Kususumi Jinja, a Shikinaisha, was merged in 1909. Formerly the ujigami of Kyū坂 Village, it was located about where Makinohommachi 1-chome 7 is now. Its deity was “Kususumi no Ōkami.” The shrine’s signpost now stands in the woods within Katano Jinja. The relationship between this shrine and a similarly named shrine in Yamato Province is unknown. === Aterui and More’s Mound === Adjacent north of the shrine grounds is Makino Park, formerly part of the shrine’s land. A mound in the center of this park is traditionally said to be the Kofun (head mound) of Aterui (Aterui no kubizuka).{{Cite book|language=ja|editor=Hirakata City Board of Education|title=Tanoshiku Manabu Hirakata no Rekishi (Enjoyable Study of Hirakata’s History)|publisher=Hirakata City Board of Education|year=2006-03-31|id=JP:21124110}} In 1979, the Kahoku Shinpo newspaper reported that local tradition has long held that a major defeated general’s head was buried here, and about 1 km northeast in Uyama-chō, another old mound was found with similar legends.{{Cite news|language=ja|title=Is the Emishi chieftain buried here? Aterui’s execution site and burial place found in Osaka’s Hirakata; Locals strive to preserve it|newspaper=Kahoku Shinpo|date=1979-03-25|edition=12th|page=18}} In 2007, a stone monument reading “Den Aterui More no Zuka” (Mound of Aterui and More) was erected. The shrine also sells Aterui omamori charms symbolizing friendship and ties, referencing the legendary stories of friendship and rivalry between Aterui and Sakanoue no Tamuramaro. == Buildings and Cultural Properties == * Honden (main hall) (Important Cultural Property) - Rebuilt in Keichō 7 (1602) by Toyotomi Hideyori with Katagiri Katsumoto as overseer. A sangensha nagare-zukuri style, hinoki cypress bark roof.{{Cite book|language=ja|title=Hirakata-shi no Shaji Kenchiku (Temple and Shrine Architecture in Hirakata)|publisher=Hirakata City Board of Education|series=Hirakata City Building Survey Report III|year=1994-03-31|id=JP:97035268|pages=34-40|chapter=Katano Jinja}} * Haiden (Worship Hall) - Also rebuilt by Toyotomi Hideyori in Keichō 7 (1602). * Stone lantern (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - From the late Kamakura period, believed to belong to the former Jingū-ji of the shrine. * East Gate (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - Also called Kuro-mon. A Yotsuashimon (four-legged gate) originally built in the late Muromachi period. * South Gate (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - Also called Aka-mon. Rebuilt by Toyotomi Hideyori in Keichō 7 (1602) as a yotsuashimon with hongawara roofing. Hirakata_Katano_Shrine_Honden.jpeg|Honden (Important Cultural Property) Katano-jinja_Haiden.jpg|Inside the Haiden Monument of Aterui in Hirakata.jpeg|"Den Aterui More no Zuka" monument == Subordinate Shrines == === On-site Subsidiaries === [[File:Katano-jinja Yorihimesha.jpg|thumb|160px|Yorihime-sha (on-site subsidiary)]] [[File:Katano-jinja Kusagamisha.jpg|thumb|160px|Kusagami-sha (off-site shrine)]] * Inari-sha - Deities: Ukemochi no Kami, Takemikazuchi no Kami, Futsunushi no Kami, Amenokoyane no Mikoto, Hime no Ōkami, [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]], Kunanodo no Kami * Yorihime-sha - Deities: Tamayorihime no Mikoto, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto, Ichikishimahime no Mikoto === Off-site Subsidiaries === Both located east of the main precincts, separated by the Hirakata East Fire Station Saka Branch: * Asahara Jinja - deity: Sarutahiko no Mikoto. Guardian for travel safety and descendant prosperity. * Kusagami-sha - deity: HiwasuSeri no Mikoto ** According to legend, when Sugawara no Michizane was en route to Dazaifu, his horse fell ill and died here, subsequently revered by locals and associated with healing skin diseases due to a pun on “kusa” (grass) and “kusa” (lesion). == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Property (National) === * Honden (including one wooden tablet) - Dated “Rebuilt in Keichō 7 (1602) 11th Month.” === Osaka Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties === * Katano Jinja: East Gate, South Gate * Stone Lantern (from late Kamakura period) == location == * location: 2-21-15 Makinosaka, Hirakata City, Osaka Prefecture == Access == * About 5 minutes’ walk east from [[Makino Station (Keihan)|Makino Station]] on the Keihan Main Line == Notes == {{Reflist|2}} == References == {{More footnotes|date=June 2024}} * Katano Jinja Ryakuki (summary booklet available at the shrine) * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Okada Momoko|title=Jinja Wakaoku Nikki: Torii wo Kugureba Betsekai (A Young Shrine Wife’s Diary)|publisher=Shodensha Kōbunko|date=2004-01|isbn=4-396-31339-X}} == Related Items == * [[Hiraoka Shrine]] - Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province == External Links == * {{Official website|https://www.katanojinja.com/|Katano Jinja}} * {{Instagram|katano_miko|Katano Jinja}} * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{Shinto Navbox}} {{Normdaten}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{draft categories| }} {{Gion cult}} {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Ichinomiya (local)]] [[Category:Katano District]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Kawachi Province]] [[Category:Go-sha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties (buildings)]] [[Category:Azuchi–Momoyama period architecture]] [[Category:Aterui]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Hirakata]] [[Category:History of Hirakata]] [[Category:Gion shrines]] [[Category:Gō-sha]] [[Category:Gion cult]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Katano Shrine]] [[Category:not stubs]] [[Category:Pages from everybodywiki under right title]] [[Category:New]] }} [[en:draft:Katano Shrine]] [[en:Katano Shrine]] [[sn:Katano Shrine]] [[ja:片埜神社]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Katano Jinja}}

Haiden (worship hall) | caption = | map_type = Japan Osaka | coordinates = {{Coord|34|50|30.5|N|135|40|03.5|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Katano Jinja}} | location = 2-21-15 Makinosaka, {{ill|Hirakata, Osaka|ja|枚方市|lt=Hirakata City|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|lt=Osaka Prefecture|12=draft|12=draft}} | deity = {{ubl|Takehayasusanoo no Ōkami (Susanoo)|Sugawara no Michizane}} | type = {{ubl|Shikinaisha (small)|(Reputed) Kawashū Ichinomiya|Former Gōsha}} | founded = Era of Emperor Suinin | honden = Sangensha nagare-zukuri style | festival = October 15 | ceremonies = {{ubl|Ohitaki-sai (Mikan throwing) on Dec.13|Ebisu-sai Jan.9–11}} }} '''Katano Jinja''' (片埜神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Hirakata, Osaka|ja|枚方市|lt=Hirakata City|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|lt=Osaka Prefecture|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a Shikinaisha (small) shrine with an old shrine Rank of gōsha. It has also been referred to as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” although that refers to it being the largest shrine in the local area, not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province. == Enshrined Deities == [[File:片野神社RIMG2186.JPG|thumb|right|Torii]] * Main Enshrined Deities: Takehayasusanoo no Ōkami (Susanoo), Sugawara no Michizane * Additional deities: Kushinadahime no Mikoto, Yashima Shinumi no Kami Due to the Meiji-era consolidation of nearby shrines, several other deities have been added, resulting in multiple enshrined Hachiman gods (total of four) and others. The Kokka (family records) of the shrine’s priestly family, the Okada family, refers to it as “the tutelary of the Haji (土師) clan.” Some old references associate its deity with Nigihayahi no Mikoto or the ancestor of the Katanoinagi clan, but the shrine denies these identifications. == History == [[File:河内名所図会 交野神社.png|thumb|From “Kawachi Meisho Zue”: Katanoinagi Jinja (Katano Jinja)]] According to shrine tradition, during the era of Emperor Suinin, Nomino Sukune, a noble from Izumo, received this land as a reward for victory in a sumo match against Taima no Kehaya. He then enshrined his ancestral deity Susanoo at this location as a clan’s tutelary deity.{{Cite web|url=https://www.katanojinja.com/blank-3|title=History|publisher=Katano Jinja|access-date=2024-06-02}} During Emperor Kinmei’s time, the shrine was renamed “Katano Jinja” after the local area “Katano” (also known as “Katano” or “Kawachi”), giving rise to the name of Katano District and eventually Hirakata City. Thus, it served as the ubusuna (local tutelary) shrine of Katano District. In the mid-Heian period, after Sugawara no Michizane (a descendant of the Haji clan) was enshrined as a kami (Tenjin), he was added here as well in Tennin 4 (960). The Okada family, who serve as shrine priests, are said to be descendants of Nomino Sukune. Listed in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō as “Katanojinja, Kuwajutsu,” it was a small Shikinaisha. It once had extensive shrine lands and was famed for its cherry blossoms (“Makino no sakura”) making it a utamakura (poetic place name). Because it was a large shrine in Katano District, in the late Heian period the shrine’s name was changed to “Ichinomiya.” This led to it being known as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” but it was not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province—rather, it was the ichinomiya of Katano District. During the Genkō War (Nanboku-chō period), it was burned but later rebuilt. In the Sengoku period, it suffered damage due to involvement in battles between the Miyoshi Sanninshū and Matsunaga Hisahide but was restored in Tenshō 11 (1583) by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who regarded it as the guardian against the demon gate (kimon) for Osaka Castle. Later, in Keichō 7 (1602), Toyotomi Hideyori rebuilt the main hall and associated buildings. During the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to Gozu Tennō and was officially named “Ichinomiya Gozu Tennō.” In the Meiji era, when merging shrines in former Makino Village, it reverted to its old name “Katano Jinja” and was Ranked as a gōsha under the modern shrine system. === Meiji-era Shrines Merger === In the Meiji era, the following shrines in the old Makino Village were merged into Katano Jinja: * Awakura Jinja (Ōaza Ogura; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Kudaraō Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Kudaraō no Mikoto & Susanoo. Note: Different from the middle shrine Kudaraō Jinja) * Mikari Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Ōsazaki no Mikoto, Kudaraō, Susanoo) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Ibojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Kamijima; Deities: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]], Amaterasu Ōmikami, Amenokoyane no Mikoto) * Hachiman Jinja (Ōaza Shimojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Uyama; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Dōso Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kunanodo no Kami) * Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kususumi no Ōkami) Because of its historical role as a protector of Osaka Castle’s “kimon” direction, Katano Jinja remains revered for hōyoke (warding off evil directions) and yakuyoke (warding off misfortune). The “oni” (demon) is regarded as a symbol and guardian deity of the shrine due to these associations, leading to unique customs such as “Oni wa uchi!” (“Demons come in!”) instead of “Oni wa soto!” (“Demons out!”) during Setsubun bean-throwing rituals, and oni motifs appearing on ema and goshuin. === Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja === Kususumi Jinja, a Shikinaisha, was merged in 1909. Formerly the ujigami of Kyū坂 Village, it was located about where Makinohommachi 1-chome 7 is now. Its deity was “Kususumi no Ōkami.” The shrine’s signpost now stands in the woods within Katano Jinja. The relationship between this shrine and a similarly named shrine in Yamato Province is unknown. === Aterui and More’s Mound === Adjacent north of the shrine grounds is Makino Park, formerly part of the shrine’s land. A mound in the center of this park is traditionally said to be the Kofun (head mound) of Aterui (Aterui no kubizuka).{{Cite book|language=ja|editor=Hirakata City Board of Education|title=Tanoshiku Manabu Hirakata no Rekishi (Enjoyable Study of Hirakata’s History)|publisher=Hirakata City Board of Education|year=2006-03-31|id=JP:21124110}} In 1979, the Kahoku Shinpo newspaper reported that local tradition has long held that a major defeated general’s head was buried here, and about 1 km northeast in Uyama-chō, another old mound was found with similar legends.{{Cite news|language=ja|title=Is the Emishi chieftain buried here? Aterui’s execution site and burial place found in Osaka’s Hirakata; Locals strive to preserve it|newspaper=Kahoku Shinpo|date=1979-03-25|edition=12th|page=18}} In 2007, a stone monument reading “Den Aterui More no Zuka” (Mound of Aterui and More) was erected. The shrine also sells Aterui omamori charms symbolizing friendship and ties, referencing the legendary stories of friendship and rivalry between Aterui and Sakanoue no Tamuramaro. == Buildings and Cultural Properties == * Honden (main hall) (Important Cultural Property) - Rebuilt in Keichō 7 (1602) by Toyotomi Hideyori with Katagiri Katsumoto as overseer. A sangensha nagare-zukuri style, hinoki cypress bark roof.{{Cite book|language=ja|title=Hirakata-shi no Shaji Kenchiku (Temple and Shrine Architecture in Hirakata)|publisher=Hirakata City Board of Education|series=Hirakata City Building Survey Report III|year=1994-03-31|id=JP:97035268|pages=34-40|chapter=Katano Jinja}} * Haiden (Worship Hall) - Also rebuilt by Toyotomi Hideyori in Keichō 7 (1602). * Stone lantern (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - From the late Kamakura period, believed to belong to the former Jingū-ji of the shrine. * East Gate (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - Also called Kuro-mon. A Yotsuashimon (four-legged gate) originally built in the late Muromachi period. * South Gate (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - Also called Aka-mon. Rebuilt by Toyotomi Hideyori in Keichō 7 (1602) as a yotsuashimon with hongawara roofing. Hirakata_Katano_Shrine_Honden.jpeg|Honden (Important Cultural Property) Katano-jinja_Haiden.jpg|Inside the Haiden Monument of Aterui in Hirakata.jpeg|"Den Aterui More no Zuka" monument == Subordinate Shrines == === On-site Subsidiaries === [[File:Katano-jinja Yorihimesha.jpg|thumb|160px|Yorihime-sha (on-site subsidiary)]] [[File:Katano-jinja Kusagamisha.jpg|thumb|160px|Kusagami-sha (off-site shrine)]] * Inari-sha - Deities: Ukemochi no Kami, Takemikazuchi no Kami, Futsunushi no Kami, Amenokoyane no Mikoto, Hime no Ōkami, [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]], Kunanodo no Kami * Yorihime-sha - Deities: Tamayorihime no Mikoto, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto, Ichikishimahime no Mikoto === Off-site Subsidiaries === Both located east of the main precincts, separated by the Hirakata East Fire Station Saka Branch: * Asahara Jinja - deity: Sarutahiko no Mikoto. Guardian for travel safety and descendant prosperity. * Kusagami-sha - deity: HiwasuSeri no Mikoto ** According to legend, when Sugawara no Michizane was en route to Dazaifu, his horse fell ill and died here, subsequently revered by locals and associated with healing skin diseases due to a pun on “kusa” (grass) and “kusa” (lesion). == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Property (National) === * Honden (including one wooden tablet) - Dated “Rebuilt in Keichō 7 (1602) 11th Month.” === Osaka Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties === * Katano Jinja: East Gate, South Gate * Stone Lantern (from late Kamakura period) == location == * location: 2-21-15 Makinosaka, Hirakata City, Osaka Prefecture == Access == * About 5 minutes’ walk east from [[Makino Station (Keihan)|Makino Station]] on the Keihan Main Line == Notes == {{Reflist|2}} == References == {{More footnotes|date=June 2024}} * Katano Jinja Ryakuki (summary booklet available at the shrine) * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Okada Momoko|title=Jinja Wakaoku Nikki: Torii wo Kugureba Betsekai (A Young Shrine Wife’s Diary)|publisher=Shodensha Kōbunko|date=2004-01|isbn=4-396-31339-X}} == Related Items == * [[Hiraoka Shrine]] - It is a Shikinaisha (small) shrine with an old shrine Rank of gōsha. It has also been referred to as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” although that refers to it being the largest shrine in the local area, not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province. == Enshrined Deities == [[File:片野神社RIMG2186.JPG|thumb|right|Torii]] * Main Enshrined Deities: Takehayasusanoo no Ōkami (Susanoo), Sugawara no Michizane * Additional deities: Kushinadahime no Mikoto, Yashima Shinumi no Kami Due to the Meiji-era consolidation of nearby shrines, several other deities have been added, resulting in multiple enshrined Hachiman gods (total of four) and others. The Kokka (family records) of the shrine’s priestly family, the Okada family, refers to it as “the tutelary of the Haji (土師) clan.” Some old references associate its deity with Nigihayahi no Mikoto or the ancestor of the Katanoinagi clan, but the shrine denies these identifications. == History == [[File:河内名所図会 交野神社.png|thumb|From “Kawachi Meisho Zue”: Katanoinagi Jinja (Katano Jinja)]] According to shrine tradition, during the era of Emperor Suinin, Nomino Sukune, a noble from Izumo, received this land as a reward for victory in a sumo match against Taima no Kehaya. He then enshrined his ancestral deity Susanoo at this location as a clan’s tutelary deity.{{Cite web|url=https://www.katanojinja.com/blank-3|title=History|publisher=Katano Jinja|access-date=2024-06-02}} During Emperor Kinmei’s time, the shrine was renamed “Katano Jinja” after the local area “Katano” (also known as “Katano” or “Kawachi”), giving rise to the name of Katano District and eventually Hirakata City. Thus, it served as the ubusuna (local tutelary) shrine of Katano District. In the mid-Heian period, after Sugawara no Michizane (a descendant of the Haji clan) was enshrined as a kami (Tenjin), he was added here as well in Tennin 4 (960). The Okada family, who serve as shrine priests, are said to be descendants of Nomino Sukune. Listed in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō as “Katanojinja, Kuwajutsu,” it was a small Shikinaisha. It once had extensive shrine lands and was famed for its cherry blossoms (“Makino no sakura”) making it a utamakura (poetic place name). Because it was a large shrine in Katano District, in the late Heian period the shrine’s name was changed to “Ichinomiya.” This led to it being known as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” but it was not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province—rather, it was the ichinomiya of Katano District. During the Genkō War (Nanboku-chō period), it was burned but later rebuilt. In the Sengoku period, it suffered damage due to involvement in battles between the Miyoshi Sanninshū and Matsunaga Hisahide but was restored in Tenshō 11 (1583) by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who regarded it as the guardian against the demon gate (kimon) for Osaka Castle. Later, in Keichō 7 (1602), Toyotomi Hideyori rebuilt the main hall and associated buildings. During the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to Gozu Tennō and was officially named “Ichinomiya Gozu Tennō.” In the Meiji era, when merging shrines in former Makino Village, it reverted to its old name “Katano Jinja” and was Ranked as a gōsha under the modern shrine system. === Meiji-era Shrines Merger === In the Meiji era, the following shrines in the old Makino Village were merged into Katano Jinja: * Awakura Jinja (Ōaza Ogura; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Kudaraō Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Kudaraō no Mikoto & Susanoo. Note: Different from the middle shrine Kudaraō Jinja) * Mikari Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Ōsazaki no Mikoto, Kudaraō, Susanoo) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Ibojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Kamijima; Deities: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]], Amaterasu Ōmikami, Amenokoyane no Mikoto) * Hachiman Jinja (Ōaza Shimojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Uyama; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Dōso Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kunanodo no Kami) * Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kususumi no Ōkami) Because of its historical role as a protector of Osaka Castle’s “kimon” direction, Katano Jinja remains revered for hōyoke (warding off evil directions) and yakuyoke (warding off misfortune). The “oni” (demon) is regarded as a symbol and guardian deity of the shrine due to these associations, leading to unique customs such as “Oni wa uchi!” (“Demons come in!”) instead of “Oni wa soto!” (“Demons out!”) during Setsubun bean-throwing rituals, and oni motifs appearing on ema and goshuin. === Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja === Kususumi Jinja, a Shikinaisha, was merged in 1909. Note: Different from the middle shrine Kudaraō Jinja) * Mikari Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Ōsazaki no Mikoto, Kudaraō, Susanoo) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Ibojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Kamijima; Deities: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]], Amaterasu Ōmikami, Amenokoyane no Mikoto) * Hachiman Jinja (Ōaza Shimojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Uyama; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Dōso Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kunanodo no Kami) * Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kususumi no Ōkami) Because of its historical role as a protector of Osaka Castle’s “kimon” direction, Katano Jinja remains revered for hōyoke (warding off evil directions) and yakuyoke (warding off misfortune). It is a Shikinaisha (small) shrine with an old shrine Rank of gōsha. It has also been referred to as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” although that refers to it being the largest shrine in the local area, not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province. == Enshrined Deities == [[File:片野神社RIMG2186.JPG|thumb|right|Torii]] * Main Enshrined Deities: Takehayasusanoo no Ōkami (Susanoo), Sugawara no Michizane * Additional deities: Kushinadahime no Mikoto, Yashima Shinumi no Kami Due to the Meiji-era consolidation of nearby shrines, several other deities have been added, resulting in multiple enshrined Hachiman gods (total of four) and others. It has also been referred to as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” although that refers to it being the largest shrine in the local area, not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province. == Enshrined Deities == [[File:片野神社RIMG2186.JPG|thumb|right|Torii]] * Main Enshrined Deities: Takehayasusanoo no Ōkami (Susanoo), Sugawara no Michizane * Additional deities: Kushinadahime no Mikoto, Yashima Shinumi no Kami Due to the Meiji-era consolidation of nearby shrines, several other deities have been added, resulting in multiple enshrined Hachiman gods (total of four) and others. The Kokka (family records) of the shrine’s priestly family, the Okada family, refers to it as “the tutelary of the Haji (土師) clan.” Some old references associate its deity with Nigihayahi no Mikoto or the ancestor of the Katanoinagi clan, but the shrine denies these identifications. == History == [[File:河内名所図会 交野神社.png|thumb|From “Kawachi Meisho Zue”: Katanoinagi Jinja (Katano Jinja)]] According to shrine tradition, during the era of Emperor Suinin, Nomino Sukune, a noble from Izumo, received this land as a reward for victory in a sumo match against Taima no Kehaya. He then enshrined his ancestral deity Susanoo at this location as a clan’s tutelary deity.{{Cite web|url=https://www.katanojinja.com/blank-3|title=History|publisher=Katano Jinja|access-date=2024-06-02}} During Emperor Kinmei’s time, the shrine was renamed “Katano Jinja” after the local area “Katano” (also known as “Katano” or “Kawachi”), giving rise to the name of Katano District and eventually Hirakata City. Thus, it served as the ubusuna (local tutelary) shrine of Katano District. In the mid-Heian period, after Sugawara no Michizane (a descendant of the Haji clan) was enshrined as a kami (Tenjin), he was added here as well in Tennin 4 (960). The Okada family, who serve as shrine priests, are said to be descendants of Nomino Sukune. Listed in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō as “Katanojinja, Kuwajutsu,” it was a small Shikinaisha. It once had extensive shrine lands and was famed for its cherry blossoms (“Makino no sakura”) making it a utamakura (poetic place name). Because it was a large shrine in Katano District, in the late Heian period the shrine’s name was changed to “Ichinomiya.” This led to it being known as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” but it was not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province—rather, it was the ichinomiya of Katano District. During the Genkō War (Nanboku-chō period), it was burned but later rebuilt. In the Sengoku period, it suffered damage due to involvement in battles between the Miyoshi Sanninshū and Matsunaga Hisahide but was restored in Tenshō 11 (1583) by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who regarded it as the guardian against the demon gate (kimon) for Osaka Castle. Later, in Keichō 7 (1602), Toyotomi Hideyori rebuilt the main hall and associated buildings. During the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to Gozu Tennō and was officially named “Ichinomiya Gozu Tennō.” In the Meiji era, when merging shrines in former Makino Village, it reverted to its old name “Katano Jinja” and was Ranked as a gōsha under the modern shrine system. === Meiji-era Shrines Merger === In the Meiji era, the following shrines in the old Makino Village were merged into Katano Jinja: * Awakura Jinja (Ōaza Ogura; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Kudaraō Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Kudaraō no Mikoto & Susanoo. Note: Different from the middle shrine Kudaraō Jinja) * Mikari Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Ōsazaki no Mikoto, Kudaraō, Susanoo) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Ibojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Kamijima; Deities: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]], Amaterasu Ōmikami, Amenokoyane no Mikoto) * Hachiman Jinja (Ōaza Shimojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Uyama; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Dōso Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kunanodo no Kami) * Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kususumi no Ōkami) Because of its historical role as a protector of Osaka Castle’s “kimon” direction, Katano Jinja remains revered for hōyoke (warding off evil directions) and yakuyoke (warding off misfortune). The “oni” (demon) is regarded as a symbol and guardian deity of the shrine due to these associations, leading to unique customs such as “Oni wa uchi!” (“Demons come in!”) instead of “Oni wa soto!” (“Demons out!”) during Setsubun bean-throwing rituals, and oni motifs appearing on ema and goshuin. === Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja === Kususumi Jinja, a Shikinaisha, was merged in 1909. Formerly the ujigami of Kyū坂 Village, it was located about where Makinohommachi 1-chome 7 is now. Its deity was “Kususumi no Ōkami.” The shrine’s signpost now stands in the woods within Katano Jinja. The relationship between this shrine and a similarly named shrine in Yamato Province is unknown. === Aterui and More’s Mound === Adjacent north of the shrine grounds is Makino Park, formerly part of the shrine’s land. A mound in the center of this park is traditionally said to be the Kofun (head mound) of Aterui (Aterui no kubizuka).{{Cite book|language=ja|editor=Hirakata City Board of Education|title=Tanoshiku Manabu Hirakata no Rekishi (Enjoyable Study of Hirakata’s History)|publisher=Hirakata City Board of Education|year=2006-03-31|id=JP:21124110}} In 1979, the Kahoku Shinpo newspaper reported that local tradition has long held that a major defeated general’s head was buried here, and about 1 km northeast in Uyama-chō, another old mound was found with similar legends.{{Cite news|language=ja|title=Is the Emishi chieftain buried here? Aterui’s execution site and burial place found in Osaka’s Hirakata; Locals strive to preserve it|newspaper=Kahoku Shinpo|date=1979-03-25|edition=12th|page=18}} In 2007, a stone monument reading “Den Aterui More no Zuka” (Mound of Aterui and More) was erected. The shrine also sells Aterui omamori charms symbolizing friendship and ties, referencing the legendary stories of friendship and rivalry between Aterui and Sakanoue no Tamuramaro. == Buildings and Cultural Properties == * Honden (main hall) (Important Cultural Property) - Rebuilt in Keichō 7 (1602) by Toyotomi Hideyori with Katagiri Katsumoto as overseer. A sangensha nagare-zukuri style, hinoki cypress bark roof.{{Cite book|language=ja|title=Hirakata-shi no Shaji Kenchiku (Temple and Shrine Architecture in Hirakata)|publisher=Hirakata City Board of Education|series=Hirakata City Building Survey Report III|year=1994-03-31|id=JP:97035268|pages=34-40|chapter=Katano Jinja}} * Haiden (Worship Hall) - Also rebuilt by Toyotomi Hideyori in Keichō 7 (1602). * Stone lantern (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - From the late Kamakura period, believed to belong to the former Jingū-ji of the shrine. * East Gate (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - Also called Kuro-mon. A Yotsuashimon (four-legged gate) originally built in the late Muromachi period. * South Gate (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - Also called Aka-mon. Rebuilt by Toyotomi Hideyori in Keichō 7 (1602) as a yotsuashimon with hongawara roofing. Hirakata_Katano_Shrine_Honden.jpeg|Honden (Important Cultural Property) Katano-jinja_Haiden.jpg|Inside the Haiden Monument of Aterui in Hirakata.jpeg|"Den Aterui More no Zuka" monument == Subordinate Shrines == === On-site Subsidiaries === [[File:Katano-jinja Yorihimesha.jpg|thumb|160px|Yorihime-sha (on-site subsidiary)]] [[File:Katano-jinja Kusagamisha.jpg|thumb|160px|Kusagami-sha (off-site shrine)]] * Inari-sha - Deities: Ukemochi no Kami, Takemikazuchi no Kami, Futsunushi no Kami, Amenokoyane no Mikoto, Hime no Ōkami, [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]], Kunanodo no Kami * Yorihime-sha - Deities: Tamayorihime no Mikoto, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto, Ichikishimahime no Mikoto === Off-site Subsidiaries === Both located east of the main precincts, separated by the Hirakata East Fire Station Saka Branch: * Asahara Jinja - deity: Sarutahiko no Mikoto. Guardian for travel safety and descendant prosperity. * Kusagami-sha - deity: HiwasuSeri no Mikoto ** According to legend, when Sugawara no Michizane was en route to Dazaifu, his horse fell ill and died here, subsequently revered by locals and associated with healing skin diseases due to a pun on “kusa” (grass) and “kusa” (lesion). == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Property (National) === * Honden (including one wooden tablet) - Dated “Rebuilt in Keichō 7 (1602) 11th Month.” === Osaka Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties === * Katano Jinja: East Gate, South Gate * Stone Lantern (from late Kamakura period) == location == * location: 2-21-15 Makinosaka, Hirakata City, Osaka Prefecture == Access == * About 5 minutes’ walk east from [[Makino Station (Keihan)|Makino Station]] on the Keihan Main Line == Notes == {{Reflist|2}} == References == {{More footnotes|date=June 2024}} * Katano Jinja Ryakuki (summary booklet available at the shrine) * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Okada Momoko|title=Jinja Wakaoku Nikki: Torii wo Kugureba Betsekai (A Young Shrine Wife’s Diary)|publisher=Shodensha Kōbunko|date=2004-01|isbn=4-396-31339-X}} == Related Items == * [[Hiraoka Shrine]] - 拝殿 |所在地 = [[大阪府]][[枚方市]]牧野阪2丁目21-15 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|50|30.5|N|135|40|03.5|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=片埜神社}} |祭神 = {{Ublist| [[スサノオ|建速須佐之男大神]] | [[菅原道真]] }} |社格 = {{Ublist| [[式内社]]（小） | （称）河州[[一宮|一之宮]] | 旧[[郷社]] }} |創建 = [[垂仁天皇]]の時代 |本殿 = 三間社[[流造]] |例祭 = [[10月15日]] |神事 = {{Ublist| お火焚祭（みかん撒き）（[[12月13日]]） | えびす祭（[[1月9日]] - [[1月11日|11日]]） }} }} '''片埜神社'''（かたのじんじゃ）は、[[大阪府]][[枚方市]]にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[郷社]]。 == 祭神 == [[File:片野神社RIMG2186.JPG|thumb|right|鳥居]] * 主祭神 - [[スサノオ|建速須佐之男大神]]、[[菅原道真]] * 配神神 - [[クシナダヒメ|櫛稻田姫命]]、[[八島士奴美神]] このほか、[[明治]]時代の近隣の神社の[[神社合祀|合祀]]により以下の神が祭神に加えられている（八幡神を祀る神社が複数あったため、八幡神が計4柱祀られている）。 * [[天照大神|天照皇大神]]、[[八幡神|品陀和氣命]]、[[天児屋命|天児屋根命]]、八幡大神、[[岐の神|久那戸神]]、八幡大神、久須須美大神、[[事代主|事代主命]]など [[社家]]である岡田家の家譜には「[[土師氏|土師家]]の鎮守」と書かれている、なお、当社の祭神について『[[神名帳考証]]』には「[[ニギハヤヒ|饒速日命]]」、『[[特選神名牒]]』には「交野忌寸の祖神」と書かれているが、片埜神社側ではこれらを否定している。 == 歴史 == [[File:河内名所図会 交野神社.png|thumb|河内名所図会｢交野神社｣（片埜神社）]] 社伝によれば、[[垂仁天皇]]の時代に[[出雲国]]の豪族である[[野見宿禰]]が、[[当麻蹴速]]との[[相撲]]に勝った恩賞として当地を拝領し、出雲の[[祖神]]である[[スサノオ|建速須佐之男大神]]を祀って一族の鎮守としたのに始まるとする{{Cite web | 和書 | url = https://www.katanojinja.com/blank-3 | title = 由緒沿革 | publisher = 片埜神社 | access-date = 2024-06-02 }}。 [[欽明天皇]]の時代には、この一帯の古名で[[交野郡]]や[[交野市]]の地名の由来でもある「片埜」（片野、交野）から「片野神社」の社号を賜ったとされ、交野郡の産土社となっている。 [[平安時代]]中期、野見宿禰の後裔・[[土師氏]]の子孫である[[菅原道真]]が[[天神信仰|天神]]として祀られるようになると、[[天徳 (日本)|天徳]]4年（[[960年]]）に当社でも菅原道真が配祀された。[[社家]]の岡田家は野見宿禰の後裔であるという。 『[[延喜式神名帳]]』では「[[河内国]]交野郡 片野神社 鍬靫」と記され、式内小社に列している。かつては広大な社地を有し、「交野の御野」「牧野の桜」と呼ばれる[[サクラ|桜]]の名所として[[歌枕]]ともなっていた。 交野郡の中では大きい神社であったこともあり、平安時代後期には社名を「一宮（いちのみや）」に改めている。なお、当社は河州[[一宮|一之宮]]とも称されたが、交野郡の一宮であって[[河内国]]の一宮ではない。 [[鎌倉時代]]の[[元弘の乱]]で兵火に罹るが後に再建されている。 [[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]の[[三好三人衆]]と[[松永久秀]]の戦いに巻き込まれてしまい荒廃したが、[[天正]]11年（[[1583年]]）に[[豊臣秀吉|羽柴秀吉]]が[[大坂城]]を築城する際、当社は大坂城の[[鬼門]]の方角にあることからその鬼門鎮護の社とされ、復興された。また、大坂城天守の北東の石垣に鬼面を刻み（これは現存しない）、当社と対面させたという。 [[慶長]]7年（[[1602年]]）には[[豊臣秀頼]]が[[片桐且元]]を奉行として本殿、拝殿、南門などの社殿を再建している。この時、交野郡の一宮（牧野坂の片埜神社）である当社の他にも、二宮（舟橋の[[二ノ宮神社 (枚方市)|二ノ宮神社]]）と三宮（穂谷の[[三之宮神社 (枚方市)|三ノ宮神社]]）も大坂城の鬼門鎮護の社として修復を行ったという。 [[江戸時代]]には[[牛頭天王]]を祀る神社となっており「一宮牛頭天王」を正式名称としていたが、[[明治]]時代に旧[[牧野村 (大阪府)|牧野村]]内の神社を合祀した際、かつての「片埜神社」に復し、[[郷社]]に列せられている。 明治時代に旧牧野村内の以下の神社を合祀した。 * 粟倉神社（大字小倉。祭神：品陀和氣命） * 百済王神社（大字禁野。祭神：百済王命・素戔嗚命。中宮の[[百済王神社]]とは別） * 御狩神社（大字禁野。祭神：大鷦鷯命・百済王・進雄命） * 産土神社（大字磯島。祭神：品陀和氣命） * 産土神社（大字上島。祭神：品陀和氣命・天照皇大神・天児屋根命） * 八幡神社（大字下島。祭神：品陀和氣命） * 産土神社（大字宇山。祭神：品陀別命） * 産土神社（大字養父。祭神：品陀別命） * 道祖神社（大字養父。祭神：久那戸神） * 式内・久須須美神社（大字養父。祭神：久須須美大神） 大坂城の鬼門除けの神社とされたことから、現在でも方除・厄除の神として信仰されている。またこれらのことにより、[[鬼]]は片埜神社の象徴・守り神とされている。絵馬や御朱印には鬼面が描かれており、節分の豆まきでは「鬼は内」と唱える。 === 式内・久須須美神社について === [[1909年]]（明治42年）に合祀された式内・久須須美神社は、合祀以前は旧坂村字九頭神の氏神であった。鎮座地は当社の南東の現在の牧野本町1丁目7番地のあたりだが、住宅地となっており場所の特定は難しくなっている。祭神は神社名のままの「久須須美大神」としていた。[[神社本庁]]『平成祭礼データ』では、久須須美神は櫛御気野神・家津御子神・熊野櫛御毛奴神・熊野加武呂乃神などと異名同神としている。式内・久須須美神社の社号標が片埜神社境内の林の中に建てられている。 なお、[[大和国]][[城下郡]]にも同名の式内社（現・[[村屋坐弥富津比売神社]]境内摂社）があるが、関連は不詳である。 === アテルイ・モレの塚 === 境内の北に隣接している牧野公園はかつては当社の社地の一部で、公園敷地の中央にある塚は[[アテルイ|大墓公阿弖利爲]]の首塚と呼ばれている{{Cite book | 和書 | editor = 枚方教育委員会 | title = 楽しく学ぶ枚方の歴史 | publisher = 枚方教育委員会 | date = 2006-03-31 | id = {{JP番号|21124110}} | page = }}。 [[1979年]]（[[昭和]]54年）3月25日『[[河北新報]]』は{{行内引用|地元には古くから”戦いに負けた大物武将の首塚がある”との伝承があった……同神社から北東に1キロほど離れた同市宇山町の竹やぶでも高さ3メートル、周囲5メートルぐらいの古塚が発見され、朽ちはてた桜の古木とともに、古くから「[[蝦夷]]の統領が処刑された場所」と伝えられていることがわかった}}{{Cite news | 和書 | title = 蝦夷の統領ここに眠る？　阿弖流為処刑地と埋葬場所見つかる　地元の人々が保存　大阪枚方　古くから首塚の伝承 | newspaper = 河北新報 | date = 1979-03-25 | edition = 12版 | publisher = 河北新報社 | page = 18 }}と報道している。さらに[[2007年]]には「伝 [[アテルイ|阿弖流為]] [[盤具母禮|母禮]]之塚」の石碑が建立された。{{Main|アテルイ#枚方市のアテルイ首塚問題}} また当社では、物語などで語られる阿弖利爲と[[坂上田村麻呂]]の友情・ライバル関係といった話から、友情・結縁の御守りとしてアテルイの御守を授与している。 == 境内 == * 本殿（[[重要文化財]]） - [[慶長]]7年（[[1602年]]）に[[豊臣秀頼]]が[[片桐且元]]を奉行として再建。三間社[[流造]]、[[檜皮葺]]{{Cite book | 和書 | title = 枚方市の社寺建築 | publisher = 枚方市教育委員会 | series = 枚方市建造物調査報告III | date = 1994-03-31 | id = {{JP番号|97035268}} | pages = 34-40 | chapter = 片埜神社 }}。 * 拝殿 - 慶長7年（1602年）に豊臣秀頼が片桐且元を奉行として再建。 * 石造灯籠（大阪府指定有形[[文化財]]） - 無銘であるが[[鎌倉時代]]の作とされ、かつて当社にあった[[神宮寺]]のものと推定されている。 * 社務所 * [[伊勢神宮|皇大神宮]]遥拝所 * 東門（大阪府指定有形文化財） - 黒門とも呼ばれる。[[室町時代]]後期に作られた棟門であったが、後に改造されて四脚門とされた。四脚門、本瓦葺。 * 南門（大阪府指定有形文化財） - 正門。赤門とも呼ばれる。慶長7年（1602年）に豊臣秀頼が片桐且元を奉行として再建。四脚門、本瓦葺。 Hirakata_Katano_Shrine_Honden.jpeg|本殿（重要文化財） Katano-jinja_Haiden.jpg|拝殿内 Monument of Aterui in Hirakata.jpeg|伝[[アテルイ|阿弖流為]]・[[盤具母禮|母禮]]之塚 == 摂末社 == === 境内社 === [[File:Katano-jinja Yorihimesha.jpg|thumb|160px|依姫社（境内社）]] [[File:Katano-jinja Kusagamisha.jpg|thumb|160px|瘡神社（境外社）]] * 稲荷社 - 祭神：[[保食神]]、[[タケミカヅチ|武甕槌神]]、[[経津主神]]、[[天児屋命|天児屋根命]]、[[比売神|比咩大神]]、[[八幡神|品陀和気命]]、久那戸神 * 依姫社 - 祭神：[[タマヨリビメ (日向神話)|玉依姫命]]、[[大国主|大国主命]]、[[イチキシマヒメ|市寸島姫命]] === 境外社 === 両社とも境内地の東方にあり、枚方東消防署阪出張所を挟むように建っている。 * 朝原神社 - 祭神：[[サルタヒコ|猿田彦命]]。旅行安全・子孫繁栄の神とされる * 瘡神社 （くさがみ-） - 祭神：[[火須勢理命|火酢芹命]] ** [[菅原道真]]が[[大宰府]]へ向う途中、当地で道真の馬が病気で倒れた。回復の見込みがないため道真一行は馬を地元の人に託して出発した。馬は介抱の甲斐なく亡くなり、路傍に埋葬された。その場所は、地元の人が馬に供えた草でいっぱいになったことから、いつしか「草神様」と呼ばれるようになった。この「草」が「瘡（くさ）」と同音であることから、後に瘡（皮膚病）に霊験のある神とされるようになり、社名も「瘡神社」となった。現在の祭神は火酢芹命であるが、これは後に定められたものである。 ** 本殿がなく、拝殿の後にある池を拝む形になる。道真の馬が祀られる以前から池が信仰の対象となっていたようである。現在拝殿となっている建物は、以前は「お籠り堂」として使われていたもので、皮膚病平癒の祈願のためのお籠りが行われていた。 == 文化財 == === 重要文化財 === * 本殿 附：棟札（1枚） - 「再興慶長七年壬寅十一月如意珠日」の記がある。 === 大阪府指定有形文化財 === * 片埜神社 2棟 ** 東門 ** 南門 * 石造灯籠 - [[鎌倉時代]]末期ごろ。 == 所在地 == * 大阪府枚方市牧野阪2丁目21-15 == アクセス == * [[京阪本線]] [[牧野駅]]より東へ徒歩約5分 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist|2}} == 参考文献 == {{参照方法|date=2024年6月|section=1}} * 片埜神社略記（社務所にて頒布のもの） * {{Cite book |和書 |author=岡田桃子 |title=神社若奥日記 鳥居をくぐれば別世界 |publisher=祥伝社 |series=祥伝社黄金文庫 |date=2004-01 |isbn=4-396-31339-X |ref={{SfnRef|岡田|2003}}}} == 関連項目 == * [[枚岡神社]] - 河内国一宮 == 外部リンク == * {{Official website|url=https://www.katanojinja.com/|name=片埜神社}} - 公式ウェブサイト * {{Instagram|katano_miko|片埜神社}} * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:かたのしんしや}} 百済王神社（大字禁野。祭神：百済王命・素戔嗚命。中宮の[[百済王神社]]とは別） * 御狩神社（大字禁野。祭神：大鷦鷯命・百済王・進雄命） * 産土神社（大字磯島。祭神：品陀和氣命） * 産土神社（大字上島。祭神：品陀和氣命・天照皇大神・天児屋根命） * 八幡神社（大字下島。祭神：品陀和氣命） * 産土神社（大字宇山。祭神：品陀別命） * 産土神社（大字養父。祭神：品陀別命） * 道祖神社（大字養父。祭神：久那戸神） * 式内・久須須美神社（大字養父。祭神：久須須美大神） 大坂城の鬼門除けの神社とされたことから、現在でも方除・厄除の神として信仰されている。またこれらのことにより、[[鬼]]は片埜神社の象徴・守り神とされている。絵馬や御朱印には鬼面が描かれており、節分の豆まきでは「鬼は内」と唱える。 === 式内・久須須美神社について === [[1909年]]（明治42年）に合祀された式内・久須須美神社は、合祀以前は旧坂村字九頭神の氏神であった。鎮座地は当社の南東の現在の牧野本町1丁目7番地のあたりだが、住宅地となっており場所の特定は難しくなっている。祭神は神社名のままの「久須須美大神」としていた。[[神社本庁]]『平成祭礼データ』では、久須須美神は櫛御気野神・家津御子神・熊野櫛御毛奴神・熊野加武呂乃神などと異名同神としている。式内・久須須美神社の社号標が片埜神社境内の林の中に建てられている。 なお、[[大和国]][[城下郡]]にも同名の式内社（現・[[村屋坐弥富津比売神社]]境内摂社）があるが、関連は不詳である。 === アテルイ・モレの塚 === 境内の北に隣接している牧野公園はかつては当社の社地の一部で、公園敷地の中央にある塚は[[アテルイ|大墓公阿弖利爲]]の首塚と呼ばれている{{Cite book | 和書 | editor = 枚方教育委員会 | title = 楽しく学ぶ枚方の歴史 | publisher = 枚方教育委員会 | date = 2006-03-31 | id = {{JP番号|21124110}} | page = }}。 [[1979年]]（[[昭和]]54年）3月25日『[[河北新報]]』は{{行内引用|地元には古くから”戦いに負けた大物武将の首塚がある”との伝承があった……同神社から北東に1キロほど離れた同市宇山町の竹やぶでも高さ3メートル、周囲5メートルぐらいの古塚が発見され、朽ちはてた桜の古木とともに、古くから「[[蝦夷]]の統領が処刑された場所」と伝えられていることがわかった}}{{Cite news | 和書 | title = 蝦夷の統領ここに眠る？　阿弖流為処刑地と埋葬場所見つかる　地元の人々が保存　大阪枚方　古くから首塚の伝承 | newspaper = 河北新報 | date = 1979-03-25 | edition = 12版 | publisher = 河北新報社 | page = 18 }}と報道している。さらに[[2007年]]には「伝 [[アテルイ|阿弖流為]] [[盤具母禮|母禮]]之塚」の石碑が建立された。{{Main|アテルイ#枚方市のアテルイ首塚問題}} また当社では、物語などで語られる阿弖利爲と[[坂上田村麻呂]]の友情・ライバル関係といった話から、友情・結縁の御守りとしてアテルイの御守を授与している。 == 境内 == * 本殿（[[重要文化財]]） - [[慶長]]7年（[[1602年]]）に[[豊臣秀頼]]が[[片桐且元]]を奉行として再建。三間社[[流造]]、[[檜皮葺]]{{Cite book | 和書 | title = 枚方市の社寺建築 | publisher = 枚方市教育委員会 | series = 枚方市建造物調査報告III | date = 1994-03-31 | id = {{JP番号|97035268}} | pages = 34-40 | chapter = 片埜神社 }}。 * 拝殿 - 慶長7年（1602年）に豊臣秀頼が片桐且元を奉行として再建。 * 石造灯籠（大阪府指定有形[[文化財]]） - 無銘であるが[[鎌倉時代]]の作とされ、かつて当社にあった[[神宮寺]]のものと推定されている。 * 社務所 * [[伊勢神宮|皇大神宮]]遥拝所 * 東門（大阪府指定有形文化財） - 黒門とも呼ばれる。[[室町時代]]後期に作られた棟門であったが、後に改造されて四脚門とされた。四脚門、本瓦葺。 * 南門（大阪府指定有形文化財） - 正門。赤門とも呼ばれる。慶長7年（1602年）に豊臣秀頼が片桐且元を奉行として再建。四脚門、本瓦葺。 Hirakata_Katano_Shrine_Honden.jpeg|本殿（重要文化財） Katano-jinja_Haiden.jpg|拝殿内 Monument of Aterui in Hirakata.jpeg|伝[[アテルイ|阿弖流為]]・[[盤具母禮|母禮]]之塚 == 摂末社 == === 境内社 === [[File:Katano-jinja Yorihimesha.jpg|thumb|160px|依姫社（境内社）]] [[File:Katano-jinja Kusagamisha.jpg|thumb|160px|瘡神社（境外社）]] * 稲荷社 - 祭神：[[保食神]]、[[タケミカヅチ|武甕槌神]]、[[経津主神]]、[[天児屋命|天児屋根命]]、[[比売神|比咩大神]]、[[八幡神|品陀和気命]]、久那戸神 * 依姫社 - 祭神：[[タマヨリビメ (日向神話)|玉依姫命]]、[[大国主|大国主命]]、[[イチキシマヒメ|市寸島姫命]] === 境外社 === 両社とも境内地の東方にあり、枚方東消防署阪出張所を挟むように建っている。 * 朝原神社 - 祭神：[[サルタヒコ|猿田彦命]]。旅行安全・子孫繁栄の神とされる * 瘡神社 （くさがみ-） - 祭神：[[火須勢理命|火酢芹命]] ** [[菅原道真]]が[[大宰府]]へ向う途中、当地で道真の馬が病気で倒れた。回復の見込みがないため道真一行は馬を地元の人に託して出発した。馬は介抱の甲斐なく亡くなり、路傍に埋葬された。その場所は、地元の人が馬に供えた草でいっぱいになったことから、いつしか「草神様」と呼ばれるようになった。この「草」が「瘡（くさ）」と同音であることから、後に瘡（皮膚病）に霊験のある神とされるようになり、社名も「瘡神社」となった。現在の祭神は火酢芹命であるが、これは後に定められたものである。 ** 本殿がなく、拝殿の後にある池を拝む形になる。道真の馬が祀られる以前から池が信仰の対象となっていたようである。現在拝殿となっている建物は、以前は「お籠り堂」として使われていたもので、皮膚病平癒の祈願のためのお籠りが行われていた。 == 文化財 == === 重要文化財 === * 本殿 附：棟札（1枚） - 「再興慶長七年壬寅十一月如意珠日」の記がある。 === 大阪府指定有形文化財 === Haiden (worship hall) | caption = | map_type = Japan Osaka | coordinates = {{Coord|34|50|30.5|N|135|40|03.5|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Katano Jinja}} | location = 2-21-15 Makinosaka, {{ill|Hirakata, Osaka|ja|枚方市|lt=Hirakata City}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|lt=Osaka Prefecture}} | deity = {{ubl|Takehayasusanoo no Ōkami (Susanoo)|Sugawara no Michizane}} | type = {{ubl|Shikinaisha (small)|(Reputed) Kawashū Ichinomiya|Former Gōsha}} | founded = Era of Emperor Suinin | honden = Sangensha nagare-zukuri style | festival = October 15 | ceremonies = {{ubl|Ohitaki-sai (Mikan throwing) on Dec.13|Ebisu-sai Jan.9–11}} }} '''Katano Jinja''' (片埜神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Hirakata, Osaka|ja|枚方市|lt=Hirakata City}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}, Japan. It is a Shikinaisha (small) shrine with an old shrine Rank of gōsha. It has also been referred to as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” although that refers to it being the largest shrine in the local area, not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province. == Enshrined Deities == [[File:片野神社RIMG2186.JPG|thumb|right|Torii]] * Main Enshrined Deities: Takehayasusanoo no Ōkami (Susanoo), Sugawara no Michizane * Additional deities: Kushinadahime no Mikoto, Yashima Shinumi no Kami Due to the Meiji-era consolidation of nearby shrines, several other deities have been added, resulting in multiple enshrined Hachiman gods (total of four) and others. The Kokka (family records) of the shrine’s priestly family, the Okada family, refers to it as “the tutelary of the Haji (土師) clan.” Some old references associate its deity with Nigihayahi no Mikoto or the ancestor of the Katanoinagi clan, but the shrine denies these identifications. == History == [[File:河内名所図会 交野神社.png|thumb|From “Kawachi Meisho Zue”: Katanoinagi Jinja (Katano Jinja)]] According to shrine tradition, during the era of Emperor Suinin, Nomino Sukune, a noble from Izumo, received this land as a reward for victory in a sumo match against Taima no Kehaya. He then enshrined his ancestral deity Susanoo at this location as a clan’s tutelary deity.{{Cite web|url=https://www.katanojinja.com/blank-3|title=History|publisher=Katano Jinja|access-date=2024-06-02}} During Emperor Kinmei’s time, the shrine was renamed “Katano Jinja” after the local area “Katano” (also known as “Katano” or “Kawachi”), giving rise to the name of Katano District and eventually Hirakata City. Thus, it served as the ubusuna (local tutelary) shrine of Katano District. In the mid-Heian period, after Sugawara no Michizane (a descendant of the Haji clan) was enshrined as a kami (Tenjin), he was added here as well in Tennin 4 (960). The Okada family, who serve as shrine priests, are said to be descendants of Nomino Sukune. Listed in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō as “Katanojinja, Kuwajutsu,” it was a small Shikinaisha. It once had extensive shrine lands and was famed for its cherry blossoms (“Makino no sakura”) making it a utamakura (poetic place name). Because it was a large shrine in Katano District, in the late Heian period the shrine’s name was changed to “Ichinomiya.” This led to it being known as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” but it was not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province—rather, it was the ichinomiya of Katano District. During the Genkō War (Nanboku-chō period), it was burned but later rebuilt. In the Sengoku period, it suffered damage due to involvement in battles between the Miyoshi Sanninshū and Matsunaga Hisahide but was restored in Tenshō 11 (1583) by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who regarded it as the guardian against the demon gate (kimon) for Osaka Castle. Later, in Keichō 7 (1602), Toyotomi Hideyori rebuilt the main hall and associated buildings. During the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to Gozu Tennō and was officially named “Ichinomiya Gozu Tennō.” In the Meiji era, when merging shrines in former Makino Village, it reverted to its old name “Katano Jinja” and was Ranked as a gōsha under the modern shrine system. === Meiji-era Shrines Merger === In the Meiji era, the following shrines in the old Makino Village were merged into Katano Jinja: * Awakura Jinja (Ōaza Ogura; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Kudaraō Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Kudaraō no Mikoto & Susanoo. Note: Different from the middle shrine Kudaraō Jinja) * Mikari Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Ōsazaki no Mikoto, Kudaraō, Susanoo) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Ibojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Kamijima; Deities: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]], Amaterasu Ōmikami, Amenokoyane no Mikoto) * Hachiman Jinja (Ōaza Shimojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Uyama; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Dōso Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kunanodo no Kami) * Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kususumi no Ōkami) Because of its historical role as a protector of Osaka Castle’s “kimon” direction, Katano Jinja remains revered for hōyoke (warding off evil directions) and yakuyoke (warding off misfortune). The “oni” (demon) is regarded as a symbol and guardian deity of the shrine due to these associations, leading to unique customs such as “Oni wa uchi!” (“Demons come in!”) instead of “Oni wa soto!” (“Demons out!”) during Setsubun bean-throwing rituals, and oni motifs appearing on ema and goshuin. === Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja === Kususumi Jinja, a Shikinaisha, was merged in 1909. Formerly the ujigami of Kyū坂 Village, it was located about where Makinohommachi 1-chome 7 is now. Its deity was “Kususumi no Ōkami.” The shrine’s signpost now stands in the woods within Katano Jinja. The relationship between this shrine and a similarly named shrine in Yamato Province is unknown. === Aterui and More’s Mound === Adjacent north of the shrine grounds is Makino Park, formerly part of the shrine’s land. A mound in the center of this park is traditionally said to be the Kofun (head mound) of Aterui (Aterui no kubizuka).{{Cite book|language=ja|editor=Hirakata City Board of Education|title=Tanoshiku Manabu Hirakata no Rekishi (Enjoyable Study of Hirakata’s History)|publisher=Hirakata City Board of Education|year=2006-03-31|id=JP:21124110}} In 1979, the Kahoku Shinpo newspaper reported that local tradition has long held that a major defeated general’s head was buried here, and about 1 km northeast in Uyama-chō, another old mound was found with similar legends.{{Cite news|language=ja|title=Is the Emishi chieftain buried here? Aterui’s execution site and burial place found in Osaka’s Hirakata; Locals strive to preserve it|newspaper=Kahoku Shinpo|date=1979-03-25|edition=12th|page=18}} In 2007, a stone monument reading “Den Aterui More no Zuka” (Mound of Aterui and More) was erected. The shrine also sells Aterui omamori charms symbolizing friendship and ties, referencing the legendary stories of friendship and rivalry between Aterui and Sakanoue no Tamuramaro. == Buildings and Cultural Properties == * Honden (main hall) (Important Cultural Property) - Rebuilt in Keichō 7 (1602) by Toyotomi Hideyori with Katagiri Katsumoto as overseer. A sangensha nagare-zukuri style, hinoki cypress bark roof.{{Cite book|language=ja|title=Hirakata-shi no Shaji Kenchiku (Temple and Shrine Architecture in Hirakata)|publisher=Hirakata City Board of Education|series=Hirakata City Building Survey Report III|year=1994-03-31|id=JP:97035268|pages=34-40|chapter=Katano Jinja}} * Haiden (Worship Hall) - Also rebuilt by Toyotomi Hideyori in Keichō 7 (1602). * Stone lantern (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - From the late Kamakura period, believed to belong to the former Jingū-ji of the shrine. * East Gate (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - Also called Kuro-mon. A Yotsuashimon (four-legged gate) originally built in the late Muromachi period. * South Gate (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - Also called Aka-mon. Rebuilt by Toyotomi Hideyori in Keichō 7 (1602) as a yotsuashimon with hongawara roofing. Hirakata_Katano_Shrine_Honden.jpeg|Honden (Important Cultural Property) Katano-jinja_Haiden.jpg|Inside the Haiden Monument of Aterui in Hirakata.jpeg|"Den Aterui More no Zuka" monument == Subordinate Shrines == === On-site Subsidiaries === [[File:Katano-jinja Yorihimesha.jpg|thumb|160px|Yorihime-sha (on-site subsidiary)]] [[File:Katano-jinja Kusagamisha.jpg|thumb|160px|Kusagami-sha (off-site shrine)]] * Inari-sha - Deities: Ukemochi no Kami, Takemikazuchi no Kami, Futsunushi no Kami, Amenokoyane no Mikoto, Hime no Ōkami, [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]], Kunanodo no Kami * Yorihime-sha - Deities: Tamayorihime no Mikoto, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto, Ichikishimahime no Mikoto === Off-site Subsidiaries === Both located east of the main precincts, separated by the Hirakata East Fire Station Saka Branch: * Asahara Jinja - deity: Sarutahiko no Mikoto. Haiden (worship hall) | caption = | map_type = Japan Osaka | coordinates = {{Coord|34|50|30.5|N|135|40|03.5|E|region:JP-27_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Katano Jinja}} | location = 2-21-15 Makinosaka, {{ill|Hirakata, Osaka|ja|枚方市|lt=Hirakata City|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|lt=Osaka Prefecture|12=draft}} | deity = {{ubl|Takehayasusanoo no Ōkami (Susanoo)|Sugawara no Michizane}} | type = {{ubl|Shikinaisha (small)|(Reputed) Kawashū Ichinomiya|Former Gōsha}} | founded = Era of Emperor Suinin | honden = Sangensha nagare-zukuri style | festival = October 15 | ceremonies = {{ubl|Ohitaki-sai (Mikan throwing) on Dec.13|Ebisu-sai Jan.9–11}} }} '''Katano Jinja''' (片埜神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Hirakata, Osaka|ja|枚方市|lt=Hirakata City|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|lt=Osaka Prefecture|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a Shikinaisha (small) shrine with an old shrine Rank of gōsha. It has also been referred to as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” although that refers to it being the largest shrine in the local area, not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province. == Enshrined Deities == [[File:片野神社RIMG2186.JPG|thumb|right|Torii]] * Main Enshrined Deities: Takehayasusanoo no Ōkami (Susanoo), Sugawara no Michizane * Additional deities: Kushinadahime no Mikoto, Yashima Shinumi no Kami Due to the Meiji-era consolidation of nearby shrines, several other deities have been added, resulting in multiple enshrined Hachiman gods (total of four) and others. The Kokka (family records) of the shrine’s priestly family, the Okada family, refers to it as “the tutelary of the Haji (土師) clan.” Some old references associate its deity with Nigihayahi no Mikoto or the ancestor of the Katanoinagi clan, but the shrine denies these identifications. == History == [[File:河内名所図会 交野神社.png|thumb|From “Kawachi Meisho Zue”: Katanoinagi Jinja (Katano Jinja)]] According to shrine tradition, during the era of Emperor Suinin, Nomino Sukune, a noble from Izumo, received this land as a reward for victory in a sumo match against Taima no Kehaya. He then enshrined his ancestral deity Susanoo at this location as a clan’s tutelary deity.{{Cite web|url=https://www.katanojinja.com/blank-3|title=History|publisher=Katano Jinja|access-date=2024-06-02}} During Emperor Kinmei’s time, the shrine was renamed “Katano Jinja” after the local area “Katano” (also known as “Katano” or “Kawachi”), giving rise to the name of Katano District and eventually Hirakata City. Thus, it served as the ubusuna (local tutelary) shrine of Katano District. In the mid-Heian period, after Sugawara no Michizane (a descendant of the Haji clan) was enshrined as a kami (Tenjin), he was added here as well in Tennin 4 (960). The Okada family, who serve as shrine priests, are said to be descendants of Nomino Sukune. Listed in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō as “Katanojinja, Kuwajutsu,” it was a small Shikinaisha. It once had extensive shrine lands and was famed for its cherry blossoms (“Makino no sakura”) making it a utamakura (poetic place name). Because it was a large shrine in Katano District, in the late Heian period the shrine’s name was changed to “Ichinomiya.” This led to it being known as the “Kawashū Ichinomiya,” but it was not the official Ichinomiya of Kawachi Province—rather, it was the ichinomiya of Katano District. During the Genkō War (Nanboku-chō period), it was burned but later rebuilt. In the Sengoku period, it suffered damage due to involvement in battles between the Miyoshi Sanninshū and Matsunaga Hisahide but was restored in Tenshō 11 (1583) by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who regarded it as the guardian against the demon gate (kimon) for Osaka Castle. Later, in Keichō 7 (1602), Toyotomi Hideyori rebuilt the main hall and associated buildings. During the Edo period, the shrine was dedicated to Gozu Tennō and was officially named “Ichinomiya Gozu Tennō.” In the Meiji era, when merging shrines in former Makino Village, it reverted to its old name “Katano Jinja” and was Ranked as a gōsha under the modern shrine system. === Meiji-era Shrines Merger === In the Meiji era, the following shrines in the old Makino Village were merged into Katano Jinja: * Awakura Jinja (Ōaza Ogura; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Kudaraō Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Kudaraō no Mikoto & Susanoo. Note: Different from the middle shrine Kudaraō Jinja) * Mikari Jinja (Ōaza Kinno; deity: Ōsazaki no Mikoto, Kudaraō, Susanoo) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Ibojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Kamijima; Deities: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]], Amaterasu Ōmikami, Amenokoyane no Mikoto) * Hachiman Jinja (Ōaza Shimojima; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Uyama; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Ubusuna Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]]) * Dōso Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kunanodo no Kami) * Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja (Ōaza Yabu; deity: Kususumi no Ōkami) Because of its historical role as a protector of Osaka Castle’s “kimon” direction, Katano Jinja remains revered for hōyoke (warding off evil directions) and yakuyoke (warding off misfortune). The “oni” (demon) is regarded as a symbol and guardian deity of the shrine due to these associations, leading to unique customs such as “Oni wa uchi!” (“Demons come in!”) instead of “Oni wa soto!” (“Demons out!”) during Setsubun bean-throwing rituals, and oni motifs appearing on ema and goshuin. === Shikinaisha Kususumi Jinja === Kususumi Jinja, a Shikinaisha, was merged in 1909. Formerly the ujigami of Kyū坂 Village, it was located about where Makinohommachi 1-chome 7 is now. Its deity was “Kususumi no Ōkami.” The shrine’s signpost now stands in the woods within Katano Jinja. The relationship between this shrine and a similarly named shrine in Yamato Province is unknown. === Aterui and More’s Mound === Adjacent north of the shrine grounds is Makino Park, formerly part of the shrine’s land. A mound in the center of this park is traditionally said to be the Kofun (head mound) of Aterui (Aterui no kubizuka).{{Cite book|language=ja|editor=Hirakata City Board of Education|title=Tanoshiku Manabu Hirakata no Rekishi (Enjoyable Study of Hirakata’s History)|publisher=Hirakata City Board of Education|year=2006-03-31|id=JP:21124110}} In 1979, the Kahoku Shinpo newspaper reported that local tradition has long held that a major defeated general’s head was buried here, and about 1 km northeast in Uyama-chō, another old mound was found with similar legends.{{Cite news|language=ja|title=Is the Emishi chieftain buried here? Aterui’s execution site and burial place found in Osaka’s Hirakata; Locals strive to preserve it|newspaper=Kahoku Shinpo|date=1979-03-25|edition=12th|page=18}} In 2007, a stone monument reading “Den Aterui More no Zuka” (Mound of Aterui and More) was erected. The shrine also sells Aterui omamori charms symbolizing friendship and ties, referencing the legendary stories of friendship and rivalry between Aterui and Sakanoue no Tamuramaro. == Buildings and Cultural Properties == * Honden (main hall) (Important Cultural Property) - Rebuilt in Keichō 7 (1602) by Toyotomi Hideyori with Katagiri Katsumoto as overseer. A sangensha nagare-zukuri style, hinoki cypress bark roof.{{Cite book|language=ja|title=Hirakata-shi no Shaji Kenchiku (Temple and Shrine Architecture in Hirakata)|publisher=Hirakata City Board of Education|series=Hirakata City Building Survey Report III|year=1994-03-31|id=JP:97035268|pages=34-40|chapter=Katano Jinja}} * Haiden (Worship Hall) - Also rebuilt by Toyotomi Hideyori in Keichō 7 (1602). * Stone lantern (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - From the late Kamakura period, believed to belong to the former Jingū-ji of the shrine. * East Gate (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - Also called Kuro-mon. A Yotsuashimon (four-legged gate) originally built in the late Muromachi period. * South Gate (Osaka Pref. Tangible Cultural Property) - Also called Aka-mon. Rebuilt by Toyotomi Hideyori in Keichō 7 (1602) as a yotsuashimon with hongawara roofing. Hirakata_Katano_Shrine_Honden.jpeg|Honden (Important Cultural Property) Katano-jinja_Haiden.jpg|Inside the Haiden Monument of Aterui in Hirakata.jpeg|"Den Aterui More no Zuka" monument == Subordinate Shrines == === On-site Subsidiaries === [[File:Katano-jinja Yorihimesha.jpg|thumb|160px|Yorihime-sha (on-site subsidiary)]] [[File:Katano-jinja Kusagamisha.jpg|thumb|160px|Kusagami-sha (off-site shrine)]] * Inari-sha - Deities: Ukemochi no Kami, Takemikazuchi no Kami, Futsunushi no Kami, Amenokoyane no Mikoto, Hime no Ōkami, [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]], Kunanodo no Kami * Yorihime-sha - Deities: Tamayorihime no Mikoto, Ōkuninushi no Mikoto, Ichikishimahime no Mikoto === Off-site Subsidiaries === Both located east of the main precincts, separated by the Hirakata East Fire Station Saka Branch: * Asahara Jinja - deity: Sarutahiko no Mikoto. Guardian for travel safety and descendant prosperity. * Kusagami-sha - deity: HiwasuSeri no Mikoto ** According to legend, when Sugawara no Michizane was en route to Dazaifu, his horse fell ill and died here, subsequently revered by locals and associated with healing skin diseases due to a pun on “kusa” (grass) and “kusa” (lesion). == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Property (National) === * Honden (including one wooden tablet) - Dated “Rebuilt in Keichō 7 (1602) 11th Month.” === Osaka Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties === * Katano Jinja: East Gate, South Gate * Stone Lantern (from late Kamakura period) == location == * location: 2-21-15 Makinosaka, Hirakata City, Osaka Prefecture == Access == * About 5 minutes’ walk east from [[Makino Station (Keihan)|Makino Station]] on the Keihan Main Line == Notes == {{Reflist|2}} == References == {{More footnotes|date=June 2024}} * Katano Jinja Ryakuki (summary booklet available at the shrine) * {{Cite book|language=ja|author=Okada Momoko|title=Jinja Wakaoku Nikki: Torii wo Kugureba Betsekai (A Young Shrine Wife’s Diary)|publisher=Shodensha Kōbunko|date=2004-01|isbn=4-396-31339-X}} == Related Items == * [[Hiraoka Shrine]] -
